analysis.investment_thesis: Fabtech is a niche turnkey cleanroom EPC play for Indian pharma/biotech capex — textbook small-cap (270 Cr mcap, 68.5% promoter) riding a real structural tailwind. But at P/E 27.6x with lumpy revenue, weak OCF-to-PAT conversion, and only 11% revenue CAGR, it doesn't yet earn a conviction buy in the SMILE framework.
key_strengths: Classic SMILE size: 270 Cr mcap in underpenetrated pharma cleanroom EPC niche benefiting from India's pharma capex + China+1
Promoter holding a healthy 68.49%, near-zero net debt (borrowings 10 Cr vs equity 95 Cr), ROCE 21.2%
FY25 inflection: Revenue 97→150 Cr (+55%), PAT 6→13 Cr (+117%), equity 52→95 Cr post fund-raise for capacity
key_risks: P/E 27.6x is rich for an EPC/project business with lumpy order-book-driven revenue (FY24 dipped to 97 Cr)
OCF only 3 Cr vs 13 Cr PAT in FY25 — poor cash conversion, FCF ~0; working-capital heavy EPC model
5-year revenue CAGR just 11% and order book/pipeline not disclosed — transformation thesis unproven
red_flags: OCF-to-PAT divergence widening (2025 OCF 3 Cr on 13 Cr PAT)
Recent equity dilution (reserves jumped 49→83 Cr) — fresh IPO money yet to be deployed productively
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a SMILE lens, Fabtech ticks Small (270 Cr), Medium-experienced (10-yr-old, incorporated 2015), and arguably Extra-large TAM — Indian pharma is in a multi-year capex upcycle and cleanroom turnkey EPC is a legitimate pick-and-shovel play with few listed pure-plays. Promoter holding at 68.49% and near-zero leverage (D/E ~0.1) are exactly what I want. FY25's bounce (revenue +55%, PAT +117%) and the 5Y PAT CAGR of 26.6% suggest operating leverage is kicking in as scale builds.

However, entry price matters enormously in small-caps and P/E 27.6x on a project-revenue business that dipped 22% in FY24 is not my comfort zone — I'd want sub-20x. More worrying is cash quality: OCF of just 3 Cr on 13 Cr PAT and FCF essentially zero despite a good year. That's classic EPC working-capital drag, and it caps how much of the earnings multiple I'm willing to pay. The recent capital raise (equity 52→95 Cr, investing CF -26 Cr) is the real test — if management deploys it into capacity that drives FY26-27 revenue toward 250-300 Cr with margin expansion, this re-rates to a multibagger. Until I see that execution, it's a watch-list name, not a buy.
